46,072 km2 for -700..-651: Sennacherib 'invad[ed] and ravag[ed] Elam' in 694 and won at Halule in 691; Ulaï in 653, after which 'Susa itself was sacked and occupied by the Assyrians' (ledger, hatched from -653).

the -700 shape plus Kition on Cyprus
Phrygia's -700 shape without the Lydian kingdom of Gyges around Sardis; Gyges took the Troad with little resistance after Phrygia's collapse (Gyges page, paraphrase).

17,090 km2, -700..-676: the heartland grown 2,000 km2 eastward (to 46.5 E). The pages date no Sabaean gain in these years; Karib'il Watar is 'late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE' (Sabaeans) or 'late 7th century' (Karib'il Watar page), so the growth may be an early step of his campaigns.
694 BC (bridged): Sennacherib invades Chaldea.
694 BC (bridged): Chaldea is subjugated.

690: Luo annexed ('Luo', 690 BC, in the page's list; the Luo page: 'Conquered by Chu: 690 BC'). The Luo page names the capital 'Yicheng (宜城)', on the Han below Xiangyang, and also says 'Luo (today's Luoshan County, Henan Province)'; drawn as 35 km at Yicheng (112.26 E 31.72 N), the researcher's choice between the two.
690: Qi conquers Ji (Shandong).
690: the state of Ji (Shandong) ends in Qi's conquest (list row).
690: Chu conquers Luo.
690: the state of Luo ends in Chu's conquest (infobox).
689: the capital moves to Ying.

688: Gela founded ('Thucydides, Eusebius: 688').
688: Chu attacks and annexes Shen.
688: the state of Shen ends in Chu's conquest (infobox 'Disestablished: between 688 and 680 BCE'); it became 'an important northern county' of Chu.
684-680: Xi annexed ('Xi', 684–680 BC). Xi lay at modern Xi County east of Xinyang (researcher's placing).
684: Duke Huan of Qi conquers Tan.
684: the state of Tan ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 684 BCE').

684: Chu overthrows Xi. 'In 684 BCE, Duke Ai of Cai was rude to Xī Guī, wife of the Duke of Xī'; the Duke of Xi asked Chu to feign an attack; 'King Wen overthrew the State of Xī and married Xī Guī'; 'Sometime between 680 and 684 BCE Xi was annexed by the State of Chu.'
684: the state of Xi ends in Chu's annexation (infobox 'Disestablished: Between 684 and 680 BC'); it became a Chu county.
681: Qi conquers Sui (Ningyang).
681: the state of Sui (Ningyang) ends in Qi's conquest (list row).
679 BCE: Bartatua succeeds Išpakaia as king of the Scythians.
679 BCE: the western steppe under Scythian dominion.
the Pontic, Crimean, Ciscaucasian and Caspian steppes conquered in the 8th-7th centuries BCE, the Kuban valley seat, and the West Asian base at 'Sakez near Lake Urmia'

678: Chu conquers Deng.
